Your probability of winning the tournament.
The rake percentage only.

The chance you hit a flush.
The rake.

questions.explanation: Risk 10 to win 50 total after the call, so 10/50 = 20%. Or 10/(40+10).

choices.text: Raising large

Raising and continuing versus a caller
Raising bigger than a no-limper open

All-in by rule.
A weaker, capped range you can attack with a raise.
The same as an under-the-gun open.

Exactly the minimum
An under-raise, which is legal in no-limit
Larger, because there is more dead money

choices.text: Fold
Call
3-bet to 9bb as a bluff
All-in for 100bb

Call or 3-bet. Both are ahead of folding.
Limp after the open, which is not a legal call
All-in for 100bb as the only continue

choices.text: J4o
A5s
KTo, because it always dominates

Calling in position
Continuing versus a single normal 4-bet

Fold. Pairs cannot call a button.
3-bet to 30bb and call an all-in

Calling if you will play fit-or-fold in position
3-betting small and folding to a 4-bet
Calling and then stacking off 100bb with ace-high on a blank flop

choices.text: Fold. Jacks are a small pair.
Limp.
3-bet for value, and reevaluate a 4-bet.

choices.text: Wider than against a button open
Tighter than against a button open
Every suited hand
Only the blinds are allowed to continue

choices.text: Stack off because you called preflop
Check-raise every turn
Give up the pot unless you have a real reason to continue
The preflop call obligates you to see the river

choices.text: The button must call every open
AKo cannot be 3-bet
Position makes folding illegal
AKo is ahead of a cutoff open and should call or 3-bet

questions.explanation: This is a standard value continue, usually a 3-bet.

choices.text: The big blind already has 1bb in the pot and closes the action.
The big blind acts first postflop.
The small blind is required to call.
The big blind can only fold or all-in.

choices.text: Call every hand that is not trash, then play out of position.
Prefer 3-bet or fold over a flat.
Complete every hand because you already posted.
Fold AA so you can trap later.

choices.text: Call. The big blind defends 100% of hands.
3-bet. Seven-deuce is a standard bluff.
Fold.
All-in.

questions.explanation: A discount is not a reason to play the worst hand. 72o still folds to a button open.

questions.prompt: Button opens, you are the big blind with AJo. Folding is…

choices.text: Required, because jacks are weak.
Required, because the big blind must fold offsuit hands.
The only legal option.
Too tight. Call or 3-bet.

questions.explanation: AJo is a standard big-blind continue against a steal, unlike against a tight UTG open.

questions.prompt: UTG opens, you are the small blind with KQo at 100bb. Best default?

choices.text: Fold or 3-bet. Do not flat out of position against a tight range.
Call. Offsuit broadways must flat the small blind.
Complete, because you posted a small blind.
All-in for 100bb.

questions.explanation: KQo is dominated by an early open and plays badly as a small-blind flat.

questions.prompt: Button opens to 2.5bb, you are the big blind with 76s and 100bb. A sound continue?

choices.text: Fold. Suited connectors are never defended.
Call. You are priced in and can hit a strong flop.
All-in.
Limp, which does not apply after a raise.

questions.explanation: The big blind can defend suited connectors against a small button open and release when they miss.

questions.prompt: You are the small blind with AA. Someone has opened. Clear mistake?

choices.text: 3-betting
4-betting if they reraise small
Folding
Raising larger because you are out of position

questions.explanation: Aces are never a fold to a single open.

questions.prompt: Both blinds called a late open and the flop is multiway. You should…

choices.text: Bluff every missed flop because you were in the blinds
Stack off any pair
Ignore the extra player
Continue tighter. Multiway, bluffs and weak pairs lose value.

questions.explanation: Two blinds in the pot means you did not isolate. Make hands, do not blast air.

questions.prompt: Which continue belongs in the big blind against a button open?

choices.text: AJs
Folding AA

questions.explanation: AJs is a clear defend. Trash and folding aces are not.

questions.prompt: Small blind versus a hijack open with JTo at 100bb. The leak is…

choices.text: Flatting and playing a dominated hand out of position
Folding
3-betting and folding to a 4-bet
Noticing that you are out of position

questions.explanation: JTo does not flat well from the small blind against a solid open.

questions.prompt: The big blind is not 'defending any two cards' because…

choices.text: The big blind posted nothing
Calls are illegal from the big blind
Even with a discount, the worst hands lose more than the pot offers
The button is forced to fold if the big blind calls

questions.explanation: Pot odds widen the defend. They do not make 72o profitable against a real open.

questions.prompt: Button min-raises, big blind holds KK. What do you do?

choices.text: Fold
Call only, so you never raise kings
Complete
3-bet for value

questions.explanation: Kings 3-bet a steal. Slow-playing them from the big blind lets the button realize equity.

questions.prompt: A value 3-bet is a hand that…

choices.text: Is ahead of the opener’s continuing range and wants more money in.
Is too weak to call and has no blockers.
Must be all-in or it is not value.
Is always 72o, to balance.

questions.explanation: Value 3-bets are ahead when called: big pairs and strong broadways, widened against late opens.

questions.prompt: Which hand is a value 3-bet against a tight under-the-gun open?

choices.text: QQ
KJo
ATo

questions.explanation: Queens are ahead of a tight early open. The others are dominated or speculative.

choices.text: Any two cards, chosen at random
A hand you will stack off if you get 4-bet
A suited ace or other blocker that can fold to a 4-bet
A small pair you refuse to fold

questions.explanation: A5s-style bluffs block strong continues and can still make a nut flush when called.

questions.prompt: In position, a live 3-bet with no limpers is often about…

choices.text: The minimum raise
100 big blinds every time
Less than the original open
3× the open. Out of position, closer to 4×.

questions.explanation: Use about three times the open in position and about four times from the blinds, then add size for limpers.

choices.text: TT+, AQ+
22–55 only
Every suited hand and nothing else
Only 72o

questions.explanation: Against a late open, pairs from tens up and AQ or better are the value core. You can widen further against a loose opener.

questions.prompt: You 3-bet A5s as a bluff and a tight player 4-bets large. Best default?

choices.text: Call and stack off
Fold
5-bet all-in. Suited aces are the nuts.
Limp

questions.explanation: The bluff 3-bet did its job when a tight range reraises. A5s is not a 100bb continue against that 4-bet.

choices.text: The button opened a stronger range than UTG.
The big blind is in position.
The button opens wide, so more hands are ahead and more bluffs work.
UTG is forced to fold to any 3-bet.

choices.text: 3-bet KK for value
Fold 72o to an open
Use A5s as a occasional bluff 3-bet and fold to a 4-bet
3-bet 72o for value and call every 4-bet with it

questions.explanation: 72o is not a value hand and cannot call 4-bets.

questions.prompt: Cutoff opens, button holds AK. The 3-bet is…

choices.text: Value
A fold
A pure bluff with no showdown value
Illegal in position

questions.explanation: AK is ahead of a cutoff open and of many calls. That is a value 3-bet.

questions.prompt: You are in the small blind and 3-bet to the same chips you would use on the button. The usual fix is…

choices.text: 3-bet smaller out of position
3-bet larger out of position, about 4× the open rather than 3×
Never 3-bet from the small blind
Only limp

questions.explanation: Out of position you want more folds and a bigger pot when called, so the 3-bet is larger.

choices.text: Bluffs always go all-in and value always limps
Value hands fold to an open
Value continues against a 4-bet more often; bluffs with blockers usually fold
There is no difference

questions.explanation: QQ continues versus many 4-bets. A5s usually does not.

choices.text: Fold AK
3-bet only AA
Stop 3-betting
Widen value 3-bets. Their open contains more dominated hands.

questions.explanation: Looser opens are attacked with a wider value range, not a tighter one.

choices.text: A call of a single open
A reraise after an open and at least one caller
A limp from the small blind
A check on the flop

choices.text: Squeeze
Fold
Cold-call only. AK cannot raise.
Limp

choices.text: AA
KK

choices.text: You are in position
KJo is the nuts
Calls are illegal
You are dominated, multiway, and first to act after the flop

choices.text: Squeeze
Fold
Complete
Check preflop, which is not an option after a raise

choices.text: All-in

Fold. Suited connectors cannot call a single raise.
Squeeze all-in

choices.text: Call. More players means defend wider with any ace.
All-in for 100bb
Fold. Your ace is dominated and you are out of position multiway.
Complete the small blind

choices.text: Automatically stack off
Assume they both folded
Ignore that the pot is multiway
Bluff less. Two callers reduced your fold equity.

choices.text: Open-raising after folds
Reraising after a cutoff open and a button call
Calling one open on the button
Folding the small blind

choices.text: Position, and a hand that makes strong flops rather than one pair
The worst offsuit hand
Being first to act against an under-the-gun range
A plan to stack off ace-high

questions.explanation: Suited connectors and small pairs realize better in position than dominated offsuit hands do.

choices.text: Standard
Required multiway
A large mistake. Squeeze.
The only way to trap

questions.explanation: Kings raise for value even multiway. Flatting lets the field see a cheap flop.

choices.text: The rules require an all-in
Callers remove the dead money

The caller’s chips are already in, and you need more folds

A5s used as a bluff
JTo

choices.text: 5-bet all-in

Call and stack off with no pair
The 3-bet forces you to call any raise

choices.text: Every suited connector
The bottom of your cold-call range
72o, for balance, every time

5-bet all-in. Tens are the nuts.
Limp after the 3-bet.

Suited connectors go up in value because stacks are short.

choices.text: Must fold
Cannot be called because it is not a favorite

Folding 72o to an open
Folding JTo to an under-the-gun 4-bet

A close spot. Against a range that is only AA and KK, queens are behind.

Illegal to call

Always be all-in with A5s

A 100bb-style deep 4-bet tree
Folding AA

Limp every pair
Ignore position

Limp. Loose tables require limps from UTG.
All-in.

choices.text: Fold. The button uses the UTG range.
Open. Position and their calling still favor a late steal that can win immediately or play in position.
All-in for 200bb
Limp only

Need 300bb of equity

A limp-only range
AA or fold
A full-ring cutoff or button range, not a full-ring UTG range

Value suited connectors more and offsuit one-pair hands less
Ignore position
Open only all-in

choices.text: Fold the bottom of your continue range. Their 3-bet is strong.
4-bet all-in with 76s
Assume every 3-bet is a bluff
Call every hand you opened

choices.text: Limp and fold to a jam
Use a 100bb cold-call tree
Raise all-in or raise an amount you are willing to call off
Fold. AJo is an under-the-gun hand only.

A straddle removes position
The straddler is the button
Straddles are conceptual here: the straddle acts like a larger big blind until the engine deals them
